spec.title: Raise the digest title limit from 200 to 300 characters
spec.content:
## Build

The example-app digest cuts titles at 200 characters and two real titles were clipped mid-word last week. Raise the constant `MAX_TITLE_CHARS` to 300 in the schema and the prompt builder, and add a test with a 300-character title.

## Open choices

1. 300 or 400 characters. Default 300: the longest clipped title was 280. Changing it later is one constant.

With no verdict in 24 hours I go on with the default.

spec.title: Add `example list --json` next to the existing `--format` flag
spec.content:
## Build

Every list verb of the example CLI already takes `--format json|plain`. The `jobs list` verb is the one that does not. Add the flag the same way as in `runs list`, same output envelope, one test.

## Open choices

1. Flag name: `--format` like the others. Default `--format`; a rename later touches one file.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the default.

issue.title: jobs list has no JSON output

spec.title: Tighten the `Port` type so an adapter cannot return a bare string
spec.content:
## Build

The storage port returns `string | Result` today and two callers narrow it by hand. Make the port return `Result` only, fix the one adapter that returns a string, and delete the two narrowing blocks.

## Open choices

1. Rename `Result` to `StoreResult` while there. Default: no, out of scope; a rename later is a mechanical change.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the default.

issue.title: Storage port return type is loose

spec.title: Replan: free issue_12 and issue_14, move issue_13 behind them
spec.content:
## Plan

issue_12 and issue_14 touch disjoint files and no longer wait on issue_13. Free them to run in parallel; issue_13 now waits on both so its migration lands last. No Issue is added or dropped and no scope changes.

## Open choices

1. Whether issue_13 waits on both or only on issue_14. Default both. Changing it later is one edge.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the default.

spec.title: Add a `retry-after` header to the example route's 429 answer
spec.content:
## Build

The example `/v1/jobs` route answers 429 with no hint. Add `retry-after` with the seconds left in the window, the same way `/v1/runs` already does. One test.

## Open choices

1. Seconds or an HTTP date. Default seconds, like `/v1/runs`.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the default.

issue.title: 429 on jobs has no retry hint

spec.title: A new Home screen with a weather orb
spec.content:
## Build

A new first screen for the example mobile app: a large animated orb that shows the weather, the next three events below it and a bottom sheet for settings. No screen like it exists in the app today.

## Open choices

1. Orb animates continuously or only on open. Default continuously.
2. Events below the orb or in the sheet. Default below.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the defaults.

spec.title: Move the nightly summaries to the large model tier
spec.content:
## Build

The nightly summaries read thin on the small tier. Route them to the large tier: about 40 calls a night, roughly 12 USD a month more than today.

## Open choices

1. Large tier for every summary or only for those over 4000 words. Default every summary.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the default.

spec.title: Let the example door accept tokens without an expiry
spec.content:
## Build

The door rejects any token with no `exp` claim, and the CI job's token never has one. Accept a missing `exp` for tokens scoped to `read:status`.

## Open choices

1. Only `read:status` or every read scope. Default only `read:status`.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the default.

issue.title: CI token is rejected by the door

spec.title: Drop the legacy `events_v1` table after the copy
spec.content:
## Build

Copy `events_v1` into `events` and, in the same release, drop `events_v1`. There is no backup of the table beyond the nightly dump, which is kept 7 days.

## Open choices

1. Drop in the same release or one release later. Default the same release.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the default.

spec.title: Where the sync state lives
spec.content:
## Build

The sync state moves out of the process. Later Issues for the mobile client, the CLI and the admin page build on whatever is chosen here.

## Open choices

1. A file per user on disk, or a table in the existing database, or a separate key-value service. Default: the key-value service; moving to the database later means rewriting the client of every consumer.
2. Push or poll. Default push; poll later needs a second protocol.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the defaults.

spec.title: A read-only plan view for leads: GET /v1/projects/:name/plan
spec.content:
## Build

The example server derives every plan row's state for the owner-only `project.show` route, so a lead gets 403 and reads git history instead. Add `GET /v1/projects/:name/plan`, read-only, in the `/v1/*` read class that already covers agents; it reuses the existing query and writes nothing. A project the owner marked private answers 404 to every caller but the owner.

## Open choices

1. A new narrow route or opening the old one to agents. Default: new route, so no lead gains the owner's full view. Changing later costs one policy row.
2. Private projects 404 for a lead. Default yes. Changing later is one caller check.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the defaults.

issue.title: Leads cannot read which plan rows are open

spec.title: Workflow `example-triage-check`, shaped like `example-triage`
spec.content:
## Build

A new workflow shaped file for file like the existing `example-triage`: one journaled step, one tool-free capability call on the cheap tier, a guard in code after the step. The daily job calls it for an open item and the job closes the item only on `done` with a reason; the guard turns a `done` with an empty reason or with no evidence into `unsure`, so a guess never closes anything. A failed call fails the run and the job retries.

## Open choices

1. Guard in code or only in the prompt. Default code. Changing later removes one branch.

No verdict in 24 hours: I go on with the default.
